explanation: During the Calvin cycle, carbon dioxide is 'fixed' by incorporating it into an organic carbohydrate. One CO2 molecule (1-carbon) is attached to a 5-carbon sugar called ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP), catalyzed by the enzyme RuBP carboxylase (Rubisco). Rubisco is a highly abundant protein, comprising 20% to 50% of all chloroplast protein content. This fixation yields an unstable 6-carbon intermediate that immediately splits into two 3-carbon molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate (3PG). ATP and NADPH are then consumed to convert 3PG into glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P).

questions.q: What enzyme catalyzes the attachment of carbon dioxide to RuBP, and what percentage of chloroplast protein does it represent?
questions.exp: The notes state that 'RuBP carboxylase (Rubisco)' catalyzes this reaction and is a 'protein that makes up 20-50% of chloroplast protein content.'

questions.q: What is the immediate product when a 6-carbon molecule formed during CO2 fixation splits?
questions.exp: According to the notes, the 6-carbon molecule 'splits into two 3-carbon molecules, 3-phosphoglycerate (3PG).'
